* **Something moves in or out** (walking, pulling in arms): $\omega_f = \dfrac{I_i\,\omega_i}{I_f}$. Rim to center: $\omega_f = \dfrac{M + 2m}{M}\omega_i$.
* KE check: $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$. It drops in a "rotational collision" and rises when someone walks inward.

**Covers:** objects or people dropped, stepped or jumped onto a spinning disk, counter-rotating drops, people walking in or out.

:::

## 11.3 Counter-rotating object dropped on a disk

**Source:** Ch 11 notes, p. 3/8. 2015 Exam 2 #11.

**Idea:** $L_i = L_f$. An object spinning the **opposite** way has a **negative** $\omega$, so its angular momentum subtracts.

**Step 1: Angular momentum before and after** (1 = the bottom disk, 2 = the dropped object):

$$L_i = I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i}$$

$$L_f = (I_1 + I_2)\,\omega_f$$

**Step 2: Solve for $\omega_f$.**

$$\omega_f = \frac{I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i}}{I_1 + I_2}$$

**Notes example. Given:**

* Disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$, $M = 500$ kg, $R = 2$ m, $\omega_{1i} = +3$ rad/s.
* Ring: $I_2 = mr^2$, $m = 200$ kg, $r = 1.5$ m, $\omega_{2i} = -2$ rad/s (spinning the opposite way).

**Step 3: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_f &= \frac{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2(3) + (200)(1.5)^2(-2)}{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2 + (200)(1.5)^2} \\[8pt]
&= \frac{3000 - 900}{1000 + 450} = \frac{2100}{1450} = 1.45\ \text{rad/s}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer:** $\omega_f = 1.45$ rad/s, in the disk's original direction.

**2015 Exam 2 #11. Given:**

* Disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$, $M = 200$ kg, $R = 3$ m, $\omega_{1i} = +4$ rad/s.
* Wheel: $I_2 = 0.8MR^2$, $M = 100$ kg, $R = 2.5$ m, $\omega_{2i} = -2$ rad/s.

**Step 3: Moments of inertia.**

$$I_1 = \tfrac12(200)(3)^2 = 900\ \text{kg·m}^2$$

$$I_2 = 0.8(100)(2.5)^2 = 500\ \text{kg·m}^2$$

**Step 4: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_f &= \frac{(900)(4) + (500)(-2)}{900 + 500} \\[8pt]
&= \frac{3600 - 1000}{1400} = 1.86\ \text{rad/s}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer: e) +2 rad/s**, the nearest choice (the other neighbor is d) +1.5).

::: {.callout-tip title="3×5 notecard"}

$$\omega_f = \frac{I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i} \pm mvr}{I_1 + I_2 + I_{added}}$$

* $I_1$, $\omega_{1i}$ = the spinning platform's moment of inertia and starting spin (merry-go-round disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$).
* $I_2$, $\omega_{2i}$ = a dropped object's moment of inertia and starting spin ($\omega_{2i} = 0$ if not spinning, **negative** if counter-rotating). Leave out if there isn't one.
* $mvr$ = a person running and jumping on: $m$ = their mass, $v$ = their speed, $r$ = distance from the axis where they land. **+** if running the same way as the rim, **−** if against it. Leave out if they just step on.
* $I_{added}$ = what joins the platform: person or point mass $mr^2$, rod lying center-to-edge $\tfrac13 m\ell^2$, dropped disk $\tfrac12 mr^2$, ring $mr^2$.
* **Something moves in or out** (walking, pulling in arms): $\omega_f = \dfrac{I_i\,\omega_i}{I_f}$. Rim to center: $\omega_f = \dfrac{M + 2m}{M}\omega_i$.
* KE check: $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$. It drops in a "rotational collision" and rises when someone walks inward.

**Covers:** objects or people dropped, stepped or jumped onto a spinning disk, counter-rotating drops, people walking in or out.

:::

## 11.4 Person runs and jumps onto the rim

**Source:** Ch 11 notes, p. 4/8. 2015 Exam 2 #12.

**Idea:** $L_i = L_f$. A person running in a straight line tangent to the rim has angular momentum $L = mvR$ about the axle ($m$ = their mass, $v$ = their running speed, $R$ = the rim's distance from the axis). After landing they're a point mass at the rim, $I = mR^2$.

**Step 1: Angular momentum before and after** (MGR: $I = \tfrac12 MR^2$, mass $M$, radius $R$, starting spin $\omega_i$):

$$L_i = \tfrac12 MR^2\,\omega_i + mvR$$

$$L_f = \left(\tfrac12 MR^2 + mR^2\right)\omega_f$$

**Step 2: Solve for $\omega_f$.**

$$\omega_f = \frac{\tfrac12 MR^2\,\omega_i + mvR}{\tfrac12 MR^2 + mR^2}$$

(If the person runs **against** the rotation, $mvR$ becomes $-mvR$.)

**Notes example. Given:** $M = 500$ kg, $R = 2$ m, $\omega_i = 0.5$ rad/s; man $m = 100$ kg running at $v = 3$ m/s.

**Step 3: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_f &= \frac{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2(0.5) + (100)(3)(2)}{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2 + (100)(2)^2} \\[8pt]
&= \frac{500 + 600}{1000 + 400} = \frac{1100}{1400} = 0.786\ \text{rad/s}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer:** $\omega_f = 0.786$ rad/s.

**2015 Exam 2 #12. Given:** $M = 500$ kg, $R = 2$ m, $\omega_i = +0.7$ rad/s; child $m = 50$ kg running at $v = 10$ m/s in the same direction.

**Step 3: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_f &= \frac{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2(0.7) + (50)(10)(2)}{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2 + (50)(2)^2} \\[8pt]
&= \frac{700 + 1000}{1000 + 200} = \frac{1700}{1200} = 1.42\ \text{rad/s}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer: c) 1.4 rad/s.**

::: {.callout-tip title="3×5 notecard"}

$$\omega_f = \frac{I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i} \pm mvr}{I_1 + I_2 + I_{added}}$$

* $I_1$, $\omega_{1i}$ = the spinning platform's moment of inertia and starting spin (merry-go-round disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$).
* $I_2$, $\omega_{2i}$ = a dropped object's moment of inertia and starting spin ($\omega_{2i} = 0$ if not spinning, **negative** if counter-rotating). Leave out if there isn't one.
* $mvr$ = a person running and jumping on: $m$ = their mass, $v$ = their speed, $r$ = distance from the axis where they land. **+** if running the same way as the rim, **−** if against it. Leave out if they just step on.
* $I_{added}$ = what joins the platform: person or point mass $mr^2$, rod lying center-to-edge $\tfrac13 m\ell^2$, dropped disk $\tfrac12 mr^2$, ring $mr^2$.
* **Something moves in or out** (walking, pulling in arms): $\omega_f = \dfrac{I_i\,\omega_i}{I_f}$. Rim to center: $\omega_f = \dfrac{M + 2m}{M}\omega_i$.
* KE check: $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$. It drops in a "rotational collision" and rises when someone walks inward.

**Covers:** objects or people dropped, stepped or jumped onto a spinning disk, counter-rotating drops, people walking in or out.

:::

## 11.5 Rod dropped from the center to the edge

**Source:** Ch 11 notes, p. 5/8.

**Given:**

* MGR: a disk with $I = \tfrac12 MR^2$, $M = 500$ kg, $R = 2$ m, $\omega_i = 2$ rad/s.
* A rod with $m = 100$ kg and length $\ell = 2$ m is dropped so it lies along a radius, center to edge.

**Find:** $\omega_f$.

**Idea:** $L_i = L_f$. The rod turns about **one end** (the center), so $I_{rod} = \tfrac13 m\ell^2$ (see 10.2).

**Step 1: Angular momentum before and after.**

$$L_i = \tfrac12 MR^2\,\omega_i$$

$$L_f = \left(\tfrac12 MR^2 + \tfrac13 m\ell^2\right)\omega_f$$

**Step 2: Solve for $\omega_f$.**

$$\omega_f = \frac{\tfrac12 MR^2\,\omega_i}{\tfrac12 MR^2 + \tfrac13 m\ell^2}$$

**Step 3: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_f &= \frac{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2(2)}{\tfrac12(500)(2)^2 + \tfrac13(100)(2)^2} \\[8pt]
&= \frac{2000}{1000 + 133} = \frac{2000}{1133} = 1.76\ \text{rad/s}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer:** $\omega_f = 1.76$ rad/s. His notes write 1.77; either way, pick the nearest choice.

::: {.callout-tip title="3×5 notecard"}

$$\omega_f = \frac{I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i} \pm mvr}{I_1 + I_2 + I_{added}}$$

* $I_1$, $\omega_{1i}$ = the spinning platform's moment of inertia and starting spin (merry-go-round disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$).
* $I_2$, $\omega_{2i}$ = a dropped object's moment of inertia and starting spin ($\omega_{2i} = 0$ if not spinning, **negative** if counter-rotating). Leave out if there isn't one.
* $mvr$ = a person running and jumping on: $m$ = their mass, $v$ = their speed, $r$ = distance from the axis where they land. **+** if running the same way as the rim, **−** if against it. Leave out if they just step on.
* $I_{added}$ = what joins the platform: person or point mass $mr^2$, rod lying center-to-edge $\tfrac13 m\ell^2$, dropped disk $\tfrac12 mr^2$, ring $mr^2$.
* **Something moves in or out** (walking, pulling in arms): $\omega_f = \dfrac{I_i\,\omega_i}{I_f}$. Rim to center: $\omega_f = \dfrac{M + 2m}{M}\omega_i$.
* KE check: $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$. It drops in a "rotational collision" and rises when someone walks inward.

**Covers:** objects or people dropped, stepped or jumped onto a spinning disk, counter-rotating drops, people walking in or out.

## 11.6 Person walks from the rim to the center

**Source:** Ch 11 notes, p. 7/8–8/8.

**Given:**

* MGR: a disk with $I = \tfrac12 MR^2$, $M = 500$ kg, $R = 2$ m, $\omega_i = 2$ rad/s.
* A man with $m = 100$ kg rides on the rim and walks to the center.

**Find:** $\omega_f$ when he reaches the center, and how the KE changes.

**Idea:** "It's a conservation of angular momentum problem." His distance from the axis, $d$, goes from $R = 2$ m to $0$, so his $I = md^2$ goes from $mR^2$ to $0$.

**Step 1: Angular momentum before and after.**

$$L_i = \left(\tfrac12 MR^2 + mR^2\right)\omega_i$$

$$L_f = \left(\tfrac12 MR^2 + m(0)^2\right)\omega_f$$

**Step 2: Solve for $\omega_f$** (the $R^2$ cancels):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\omega_f &= \frac{\tfrac12 MR^2 + mR^2}{\tfrac12 MR^2}\,\omega_i \\[8pt]
&= \frac{\tfrac{M}{2} + m}{\tfrac{M}{2}}\,\omega_i = \frac{M + 2m}{M}\,\omega_i
\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3: Plug in.**

$$\omega_f = \frac{500 + 2(100)}{500}(2) = \tfrac75(2) = 2.8\ \text{rad/s}$$

**Step 4: KE before**, $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_i &= \tfrac12\left(\tfrac12 MR^2 + mR^2\right)\omega_i^2 \\[8pt]
&= \tfrac12\left(1000 + 400\right)(2)^2 = 2800\ \text{J}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 5: KE after.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_f &= \tfrac12\left(\tfrac12 MR^2\right)\omega_f^2 \\[8pt]
&= \tfrac12(1000)(2.8)^2 = 3920\ \text{J}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer:** $\omega_f = 2.8$ rad/s. The KE goes **up**, from 2800 J to 3920 J: "It took energy to move from rim to the center."

::: {.callout-tip title="3×5 notecard"}

$$\omega_f = \frac{I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i} \pm mvr}{I_1 + I_2 + I_{added}}$$

* $I_1$, $\omega_{1i}$ = the spinning platform's moment of inertia and starting spin (merry-go-round disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$).
* $I_2$, $\omega_{2i}$ = a dropped object's moment of inertia and starting spin ($\omega_{2i} = 0$ if not spinning, **negative** if counter-rotating). Leave out if there isn't one.
* $mvr$ = a person running and jumping on: $m$ = their mass, $v$ = their speed, $r$ = distance from the axis where they land. **+** if running the same way as the rim, **−** if against it. Leave out if they just step on.
* $I_{added}$ = what joins the platform: person or point mass $mr^2$, rod lying center-to-edge $\tfrac13 m\ell^2$, dropped disk $\tfrac12 mr^2$, ring $mr^2$.
* **Something moves in or out** (walking, pulling in arms): $\omega_f = \dfrac{I_i\,\omega_i}{I_f}$. Rim to center: $\omega_f = \dfrac{M + 2m}{M}\omega_i$.
* KE check: $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$. It drops in a "rotational collision" and rises when someone walks inward.

**Covers:** objects or people dropped, stepped or jumped onto a spinning disk, counter-rotating drops, people walking in or out.

# Review: Chapters 4 and 5 (both were on the 2015 Exam 2)

The professor listed Chapters 6–11 for this exam, but the 2015 Exam 2 also had one projectile question (Ch 4) and one forces-on-a-ramp question (Ch 5). They're worked here so you can find them.

## R.1 Projectile from a ledge: maximum height (Ch 4)

**Source:** 2015 Exam 2 #2. Same type as Practice Exam 2-1 #2.

**Given:** $h = 3$ m (height of the ledge above the ground), $v_0 = 20$ m/s (launch speed), $\theta = 45^\circ$ (launch angle above the horizontal).

**Find:** $H$, the highest point of the path, measured from the **ground**.

**Idea:** split the launch velocity into horizontal and vertical parts. Only the vertical motion decides the height. At the highest point the vertical velocity is zero ($v_y = 0$), while the horizontal velocity keeps going. Take up as $+$, so the vertical acceleration is $-g$.

**Step 1: Split the launch velocity.**

$$v_{0x} = v_0\cos\theta$$

$$v_{0y} = v_0\sin\theta$$

**Step 2: Vertical kinematics from the launch point to the top.** Use the equation without time, $v_y^2 = v_{0y}^2 + 2a\,\Delta y$, with $a = -g$ and $v_y = 0$ at the top:

$$
\begin{aligned}
v_y^2 &= v_{0y}^2 - 2g\,\Delta y \\[8pt]
0 &= (v_0\sin\theta)^2 - 2g\,\Delta y \\[8pt]
\Delta y &= \frac{(v_0\sin\theta)^2}{2g}
\end{aligned}
$$

$\Delta y$ is the height gained **above the ledge**.

**Step 3: Add the ledge height.**

$$H = h + \Delta y = h + \frac{(v_0\sin\theta)^2}{2g}$$

**Step 4: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
H &= 3 + \frac{(20\sin 45^\circ)^2}{2(9.8)} \\[8pt]
&= 3 + \frac{(14.14)^2}{19.6} = 3 + \frac{200}{19.6} \\[8pt]
&= 3 + 10.2 = 13.2\ \text{m}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer: c) 13.2 m.** (b) 10.2 m forgets to add the ledge.

**Same answer by energy ($E_i = E_f$, no friction).** Put $h = 0$ at the ground. At the top the mass still moves horizontally at $v_0\cos\theta$, so its KE is **not** zero there:

$$E_i = \tfrac12 mv_0^2 + mgh$$

$$E_f = \tfrac12 m(v_0\cos\theta)^2 + mgH$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tfrac12 mv_0^2 + mgh &= \tfrac12 mv_0^2\cos^2\theta + mgH \\[8pt]
gH &= gh + \tfrac12 v_0^2(1 - \cos^2\theta) = gh + \tfrac12 v_0^2\sin^2\theta \\[8pt]
H &= h + \frac{(v_0\sin\theta)^2}{2g}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Time to the top**, if it's asked: $v_y = v_{0y} - gt = 0$, so $t_{top} = \dfrac{v_0\sin\theta}{g} = \dfrac{14.14}{9.8} = 1.44$ s.

**Practice Exam 2-1 #2 with the same steps:** $h = 5.0$ m, $v_0 = 25$ m/s, $\theta = 30^\circ$:

$$H = h + \frac{(v_0\sin\theta)^2}{2g} = 5.0 + \frac{(25\sin 30^\circ)^2}{2(9.8)} = 5.0 + \frac{(12.5)^2}{19.6} = 5.0 + 7.97 = 13.0\ \text{m}$$

::: {.callout-tip title="3×5 notecard"}

$$H = h + \frac{(v_0\sin\theta)^2}{2g}$$

$$t_{top} = \frac{v_0\sin\theta}{g}$$

* $H$ = highest point above the ground (m); $h$ = launch height above the ground (m; $0$ if launched from the ground).
* $v_0$ = launch speed (m/s); $\theta$ = launch angle above the horizontal; $t_{top}$ = time to reach the top (s).

**Covers:** maximum height from a ledge or the ground, time to the top.

:::

## R.2 Sliding up a rough ramp: time to stop (Ch 5)

**Source:** 2015 Exam 2 #4. Same physics as 7.6, but a **time** question, so it needs forces and kinematics.

**Given:** $m = 5$ kg, $\mu_k = 0.6$, $\theta = 5^\circ$, $v_i = 7$ m/s sliding up.

**Find:** the time $\Delta t$ until it stops.

**Idea:** take up the slope as $+$. Going up, gravity's slope component $mg\sin\theta$ and friction $\mu_k N$ both point **down** the slope. On an incline, $N = mg\cos\theta$.

**Step 1: Forces perpendicular to the slope.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
N - mg\cos\theta &= 0 \\[8pt]
N &= mg\cos\theta
\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2: Newton's 2nd law along the slope.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
ma &= -mg\sin\theta - \mu_k N \\[8pt]
ma &= -mg\sin\theta - \mu_k mg\cos\theta \\[8pt]
a &= -g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)
\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3: Kinematics, $v_f = v_i + a\,\Delta t$ with $v_f = 0$.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= v_i - g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)\,\Delta t \\[8pt]
\Delta t &= \frac{v_i}{g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4: Plug in.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta t &= \frac{7}{9.8(\sin 5^\circ + 0.6\cos 5^\circ)} \\[8pt]
&= \frac{7}{9.8(0.0872 + 0.5977)} = \frac{7}{6.71} = 1.04\ \text{s}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Answer: b) 1.0 s.** The 5 kg mass cancels.

**Same answer with energy + kinematics.** Energy (7.6, with $v_f = 0$) gives the stopping distance, and the average-velocity equation turns it into a time:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta x &= \frac{v_i^2}{2g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)} \\[8pt]
\Delta x &= \frac{v_i + v_f}{2}\,\Delta t = \frac{v_i}{2}\,\Delta t \\[8pt]
\Delta t &= \frac{2\Delta x}{v_i} = \frac{v_i}{g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)}
\end{aligned}
$$

::: {.callout-tip title="3×5 notecard"}

$$\textbf{Up the slope:}\quad v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 - 2g\,\Delta x(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Down the slope:}\quad v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + 2g\,\Delta x(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Stops after (up):}\quad \Delta x = \frac{v_i^2}{2g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Stops after (down):}\quad \Delta x = \frac{v_i^2}{2g(\mu_k\cos\theta - \sin\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Time:}\quad t = \frac{2\,\Delta x}{v_i + v_f}$$

* $v_i$, $v_f$ = speed at the start / end (m/s); $\Delta x$ = distance **along the slope** (m).
* $\theta$ = incline angle from the horizontal; $\mu_k$ = kinetic friction ($\mu_k = 0$ for frictionless).
* **Negative under the root** = it stops first. Use the stopping-distance line.
* Sliding down only stops if $\mu_k\cos\theta > \sin\theta$.
* Time with forces instead: $a = g(\sin\theta \pm \mu_k\cos\theta)$ (+ going up, − going down), then $t = \dfrac{|v_f - v_i|}{a}$.

**Covers:** frictionless or rough inclines, sliding up or down, how fast after a distance, how far until it stops, how long it takes.

:::

# The 3×5 notecard: every formula in one place

One card per problem type. Each formula is general: it covers the variations of that problem, and every symbol is defined in its box.

## Curves (6.1–6.4)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_{max} = \sqrt{gr\,\frac{\tan\theta + \mu_s}{1 - \mu_s\tan\theta}}$$

$$v_{min} = \sqrt{gr\,\frac{\tan\theta - \mu_s}{1 + \mu_s\tan\theta}}$$

* $g = 9.8$ m/s², $r$ = radius of the curve (m).
* $\theta$ = bank angle from the horizontal; $\mu_s$ = coefficient of static friction (tires on road).
* **Flat curve:** $\theta = 0$ gives $v_{max} = \sqrt{\mu_s gr}$.
* **No friction:** $\mu_s = 0$ gives the single speed $v = \sqrt{gr\tan\theta}$.
* If $\tan\theta < \mu_s$, there is no $v_{min}$ (the car can sit still on the bank).
* **Answer choices:** round a $v_{max}$ **down** and a $v_{min}$ **up** to a choice that works.

**Covers:** flat curves, banked curves (max or min), frictionless banks. To find $\mu_s$ or $r$ instead, solve the same equation for it.

:::

## Free fall and roller coasters (7.1, 7.3)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + 2g(h_i - h_f)}$$

* $v_i$, $v_f$ = speed at the start / end (m/s); $h_i$, $h_f$ = height at the start / end (m), from any reference level.
* Frictionless only. Starting from rest: $v_f = \sqrt{2g\,\Delta h}$, where $\Delta h$ = the drop.
* If the object **rises** ($h_f > h_i$), the bracket is negative and it slows down.

**Covers:** dropped objects, roller coasters at any point on the track, frictionless slides from a height.

:::

## Halfpipe (7.4)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$h_f = h_i + \frac{v_i^2}{2g} - n\,\mu L$$

* $h_i$ = starting height (m); $h_f$ = height reached on the far side (m); $v_i$ = starting speed ($0$ if starting from rest).
* $\mu$ = friction on the rough patch; $L$ = length of the rough patch (m); $n$ = number of times it crosses the patch.
* Frictionless: $h_f = h_i$. One crossing from rest: $h_f = h_i - \mu L$.
* **Number of full crossings before it stops** = the whole-number part of $\dfrac{h_i}{\mu L}$ (from rest).

**Covers:** frictionless halfpipes, one rough crossing, several back-and-forth passes, a pushed start.

:::

## Single block on an incline (7.5–7.8, R.2)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$\textbf{Up the slope:}\quad v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 - 2g\,\Delta x(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Down the slope:}\quad v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + 2g\,\Delta x(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Stops after (up):}\quad \Delta x = \frac{v_i^2}{2g(\sin\theta + \mu_k\cos\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Stops after (down):}\quad \Delta x = \frac{v_i^2}{2g(\mu_k\cos\theta - \sin\theta)}$$

$$\textbf{Time:}\quad t = \frac{2\,\Delta x}{v_i + v_f}$$

* $v_i$, $v_f$ = speed at the start / end (m/s); $\Delta x$ = distance **along the slope** (m).
* $\theta$ = incline angle from the horizontal; $\mu_k$ = kinetic friction ($\mu_k = 0$ for frictionless).
* **Negative under the root** = it stops first. Use the stopping-distance line.
* Sliding down only stops if $\mu_k\cos\theta > \sin\theta$.
* Time with forces instead: $a = g(\sin\theta \pm \mu_k\cos\theta)$ (+ going up, − going down), then $t = \dfrac{|v_f - v_i|}{a}$.

**Covers:** frictionless or rough inclines, sliding up or down, how fast after a distance, how far until it stops, how long it takes.

:::

## Springs (7.9, 7.10)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$\tfrac12 kx^2 = \tfrac12 mv^2 + mgh$$

$$\text{Compression to stop a mass:}\quad x = \sqrt{\frac{2mgh + mv_i^2}{k}}$$

$$\text{Launch straight up:}\quad h = \frac{kx^2}{2mg}$$

$$\text{Launch along a level floor:}\quad v = x\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$$

* $k$ = spring constant (N/m); $x$ = how far the spring is compressed or stretched (m).
* $m$ = the mass (kg); $v$ = its speed when the spring is relaxed (m/s); $h$ = height above (or drop to) the spring's position (m).
* For a launch, measure $h$ from the **release point**. Frictionless only.

**Covers:** a mass sliding down into a spring, vertical spring launches, horizontal spring launches.

:::

## Power (7.11)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{mgh}{t} = Fv$$

* $P$ = power (W = J/s); $W$ = work or energy (J); $t$ = time (s).
* $m$ = mass lifted (kg); $h$ = height gained (m).
* $F$ = force applied (N); $v$ = speed it moves at (m/s), for a lift or pull at steady speed.

**Covers:** stairs, lifts, motors, pulling at constant speed.

:::

## Incline + hanging mass + pulley (7.12, 7.13, 10.6)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + \frac{2g\,\Delta x\,B}{m_1 + m_2 + \dfrac{I}{R^2}}}$$

$$\text{Stops after:}\quad \Delta x = \frac{-\left(m_1 + m_2 + \dfrac{I}{R^2}\right)v_i^2}{2gB}$$

* $m_1$ = block on the incline; $m_2$ = hanging block ($m_2 = 0$ if nothing hangs); $\theta$ = incline angle; $\mu_k$ = friction between $m_1$ and the incline.
* $\Delta x$ = distance each block moves (m); $v_i$, $v_f$ = their shared speed at the start / end.
* $I$, $R$ = pulley's moment of inertia and radius ($I = 0$ for a massless pulley; disk $I/R^2 = \tfrac12 M$).
* $B$ = the "net pull" (kg), picked by direction of motion:
    * $m_2$ falls, $m_1$ slides **up**: $B = m_2 - m_1\sin\theta - \mu_k m_1\cos\theta$.
    * $m_1$ slides **down**, $m_2$ rises: $B = m_1\sin\theta - m_2 - \mu_k m_1\cos\theta$.
* $B > 0$: speeds up. $B < 0$: slows down; a negative number under the root means it stops first, so use the second line.

**Covers:** a block on an incline tied to a hanging block, either direction, with or without friction, with a massless or massive pulley (2015 Exam #13 is $m_2 = 0$ with a disk pulley).

:::

## Loop-the-loop (7.14)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_{top,\,min} = \sqrt{gR}$$

$$v_{bottom,\,min} = \sqrt{5gR}$$

$$h_{min} = \tfrac52 R$$

$$v_{top}^2 = v_{bottom}^2 - 4gR = 2g(h - 2R)$$

$$\text{Top:}\quad N = \frac{mv_{top}^2}{R} - mg$$

$$\text{Bottom:}\quad N = \frac{mv_{bottom}^2}{R} + mg$$

* $R$ = loop radius (m); $h$ = starting height above the bottom of the loop, starting from rest (m); $m$ = mass (kg).
* $v_{top}$, $v_{bottom}$ = speed at the top / bottom of the loop; $N$ = normal force from the track (N).
* "Barely" makes it = $N = 0$ at the top. Launched from $h = \tfrac52 R$: $N_{bottom} = 6mg$.
* **Answer choices:** these are minimums, so round **up** to a choice that works.

**Covers:** minimum speed at the top or bottom, minimum launch height, normal force at the top or bottom for any launch height.

:::

## Projectile from a ledge (R.1)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$H = h + \frac{(v_0\sin\theta)^2}{2g}$$

$$t_{top} = \frac{v_0\sin\theta}{g}$$

* $H$ = highest point above the ground (m); $h$ = launch height above the ground (m; $0$ if launched from the ground).
* $v_0$ = launch speed (m/s); $\theta$ = launch angle above the horizontal; $t_{top}$ = time to reach the top (s).

**Covers:** maximum height from a ledge or the ground, time to the top.

:::

## Force from a momentum change (9.1)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$F = \frac{m(v_f - v_i)}{t}$$

* $m$ = mass (kg); $v_i$, $v_f$ = velocity before / after **with signs** (reversing direction flips the sign); $t$ = contact time (s).
* Bounces straight back at the same speed: $|F| = \dfrac{2mv}{t}$. Comes to a stop: $|F| = \dfrac{mv}{t}$.
* $mv$ alone is momentum (kg·m/s), and $m(v_f - v_i)$ is the impulse (N·s); neither is a force.

**Covers:** bounces, catches, stops, any average force from a change in velocity.

:::

## Sticking collisions (9.2)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_f = \frac{m_1v_{1i} + m_2v_{2i}}{m_1 + m_2}$$

$$\frac{K_f}{K_i} = \frac{(m_1 + m_2)\,v_f^2}{m_1v_{1i}^2 + m_2v_{2i}^2}$$

* $m_1$, $m_2$ = the two masses; $v_{1i}$, $v_{2i}$ = velocities before, **with signs** (pick a + direction).
* $v_f$ = shared velocity after they stick; $K_i$, $K_f$ = total kinetic energy before / after.
* One object at rest ($v_{2i} = 0$): $\dfrac{K_f}{K_i} = \dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2}$.

**Covers:** any objects that stick, moving the same way or toward each other; symbolic masses like $2m$ and speeds like $3v$ cancel.

:::

## Elastic collisions and the cue ball (9.3, 9.4)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_{1f} = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)v_{1i} + 2m_2v_{2i}}{m_1 + m_2}$$

$$v_{2f} = v_{1i} + v_{1f} - v_{2i}$$

* $m_1$, $m_2$ = the two masses; $v_{1i}$, $v_{2i}$ = velocities before; $v_{1f}$, $v_{2f}$ = velocities after.
* **Every velocity has a sign.** Pick + (say, right); anything moving left is negative. A negative answer means it moves left.
* Either object can be "object 1".
* Equal masses, object 2 at rest (cue ball and 8-ball): $v_{1f} = 0$ and $v_{2f} = v_{1i}$.

**Covers:** any 1-D elastic collision: head-on, catching up, one at rest, equal or unequal masses.

:::

## Ballistic pendulum (9.5)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v = \frac{M + m}{m}\sqrt{2gh}$$

$$h = \frac{1}{2g}\left(\frac{mv}{M + m}\right)^2$$

$$\frac{K_f}{K_i} = \frac{m}{M + m}$$

* $m$ = bullet mass; $M$ = block mass; $v$ = bullet speed before the hit (m/s); $h$ = height the block swings up (m).
* Block + bullet speed right after the hit: $V = \dfrac{mv}{M + m} = \sqrt{2gh}$.
* $K_f/K_i$ = fraction of the bullet's KE left in the swinging block.

**Covers:** finding the bullet speed, the swing height, the speed right after the hit, or the fraction of KE kept.

:::

## Rotational kinematics (10.1)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$\omega_f = \omega_i + \alpha t$$

$$\Delta\theta = \frac{\omega_i + \omega_f}{2}\,t$$

$$\omega_f^2 = \omega_i^2 + 2\alpha\,\Delta\theta$$

$$\Delta\theta = \omega_i t + \tfrac12\alpha t^2$$

* $\omega_i$, $\omega_f$ = angular velocity at the start / end (rad/s); $\alpha$ = constant angular acceleration (rad/s²).
* $\Delta\theta$ = angle turned (**radians**; 1 rev = $2\pi$ rad); $t$ = time (s).
* Pick the equation that leaves out the one quantity you're not given and not asked for.

**Covers:** finding $\alpha$, $t$, $\Delta\theta$ or $\omega$ for anything spinning up or slowing down at a steady rate.

:::

## Parallel axis theorem (10.2)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$I = I_{cm} + md^2$$

**$d$ = distance from the object's CENTER to the new axis**, not from its end or edge.

**Rod, axis a distance $a$ from one end:**

$$I = m\left[\frac{\ell^2}{12} + \left(\frac{\ell}{2} - a\right)^2\right]$$

**Rod about one end** ($a = 0$):

$$I = \tfrac13 m\ell^2$$

**Disk about a point on its rim:**

$$I = \tfrac32 MR^2$$

**Ring about a point on its rim:**

$$I = 2MR^2$$

**Point mass at distance $r$:**

$$I = mr^2$$

**System of pieces** (all about the same axis):

$$I_{total} = I_1 + I_2 + \cdots$$

* $I$ = moment of inertia about the new axis (kg·m²); $I_{cm}$ = about the object's own center (his $I_0$); $m$ or $M$ = the object's mass (kg).
* $\ell$ = rod length (m); $a$ = how far the axis is from the **end** of the rod (m); $R$ = radius (m); $r$ = a point mass's distance from the axis (m).
* $I_{cm}$ values: rod $\tfrac1{12}m\ell^2$, disk $\tfrac12 MR^2$, ring $MR^2$, sphere $\tfrac25 MR^2$, point mass $0$.
* **Never** add $md^2$ to $\tfrac13 m\ell^2$. That value is already about the end.

**Covers:** rods pivoted anywhere along their length, disks or rings spun about their rim, people or objects placed on a turntable, total $I$ of a system.

:::

## Rolling acceleration (10.3)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + \dfrac{I}{mR^2}}$$

* $a$ = acceleration of the center down the incline (m/s²); $\theta$ = incline angle.
* $I$ = the rolling object's moment of inertia; $m$, $R$ = its mass and radius.
* Sphere $\tfrac57 g\sin\theta$; disk $\tfrac23 g\sin\theta$; ring $\tfrac12 g\sin\theta$; sliding $g\sin\theta$.

**Covers:** acceleration of any object rolling without slipping down an incline.

:::

## Atwood's machine and hanging mass on a pulley (7.2, 10.4)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + \frac{2gh(m_1 - m_2)}{m_1 + m_2 + \dfrac{I}{R^2}}}$$

$$a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2 + \dfrac{I}{R^2}}$$

* $m_1$ = the hanging mass that **falls**; $m_2$ = the hanging mass that **rises**.
* $h$ = distance each mass moves (m); $v_i$, $v_f$ = their shared speed at the start / end.
* $I$, $R$ = the pulley's moment of inertia and radius. Copy $I$ from the problem; $R$ cancels (disk $I/R^2 = \tfrac12 M$, ring $= M$, massless $= 0$).
* **One hanging mass** (string wrapped on a pulley): set $m_2 = 0$.
* String tension on the falling mass: $T = m_1(g - a)$.

**Covers:** Atwood's machine with a massless or massive pulley, a single mass on a pulley with any shape. (A mass on an **incline** uses the 7.12 card.)

:::

## Rolling speed at the bottom (10.5)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$v = \sqrt{\frac{2gh}{1 + \dfrac{I}{mR^2}}}$$

$$\omega = \frac{v}{R}$$

* $v$ = speed of the center at the bottom (m/s); $\omega$ = spin rate at the bottom (rad/s); $h$ = vertical drop (m), starting from rest.
* $I$ = the object's moment of inertia; $m$, $R$ = its mass and radius ($R$ matters for $\omega$, not for $v$).
* Ring $\sqrt{gh}$; disk $\sqrt{\tfrac43 gh}$; sphere $\sqrt{\tfrac{10}{7}gh}$; sliding $\sqrt{2gh}$.

**Covers:** speed or rotational velocity of any rolling object at the bottom; which one wins a race (sphere, then disk, then ring).

:::

## Angular momentum (11.1–11.6)

::: {.callout-tip title="Notecard"}

$$\omega_f = \frac{I_1\omega_{1i} + I_2\omega_{2i} \pm mvr}{I_1 + I_2 + I_{added}}$$

* $I_1$, $\omega_{1i}$ = the spinning platform's moment of inertia and starting spin (merry-go-round disk: $I_1 = \tfrac12 MR^2$).
* $I_2$, $\omega_{2i}$ = a dropped object's moment of inertia and starting spin ($\omega_{2i} = 0$ if not spinning, **negative** if counter-rotating). Leave out if there isn't one.
* $mvr$ = a person running and jumping on: $m$ = their mass, $v$ = their speed, $r$ = distance from the axis where they land. **+** if running the same way as the rim, **−** if against it. Leave out if they just step on.
* $I_{added}$ = what joins the platform: person or point mass $mr^2$, rod lying center-to-edge $\tfrac13 m\ell^2$, dropped disk $\tfrac12 mr^2$, ring $mr^2$.
* **Something moves in or out** (walking, pulling in arms): $\omega_f = \dfrac{I_i\,\omega_i}{I_f}$. Rim to center: $\omega_f = \dfrac{M + 2m}{M}\omega_i$.
* KE check: $K = \tfrac12 I\omega^2$. It drops in a "rotational collision" and rises when someone walks inward.

**Covers:** objects or people dropped, stepped or jumped onto a spinning disk, counter-rotating drops, people walking in or out.

:::
